title: Subscription — renewal day, invoice, payment and cancellation
body:
The **Előfizetés** card at the top of the **Modulok** tab shows in one place what
you pay and when: the renewal day, the **„Jelenlegi díj”** and the amount of your next
invoice, with an itemised breakdown.

## Monthly or yearly payment?

There are two billing rhythms, and every field on the card speaks accordingly. To see
which one is yours, read the **„Jelenlegi díj”** field: an ending of **„/hó”** means monthly,
an ending of **„/év”** means yearly payment.

- **With monthly payment**, the **„Fordulónap”** field shows the day of the month (for example, “the 10th of every month”), and
  the fee is due every month. In this case an offer also appears beneath the card,
  with which you can switch to yearly payment — it tells you how much you would save with it.
- **With yearly payment**, the **„Fordulónap”** field shows the same day once a year
  (for example, “yearly, the 10th”), and a
  separate line also states the **„Fizetés üteme”**, including the number of gift months.
  In this case the **„A következő számla tételei”** label also shows how the
  yearly fee is made up from the monthly items.

With yearly payment you do **not pay twelve monthly fees**: you receive a few months as a gift, so
on the modules’ price tag the yearly amount comes first, in larger type, with the monthly figure faintly beneath it. The help for the **Modulok** tab
(*“How much does it cost?”*) describes this in detail.

## What is the renewal day?

Your subscription always renews on the same day — that is the renewal day (the day of your
first payment); monthly with monthly payment, yearly with yearly payment. The fee for every module arrives on **one
shared invoice**; there are no scattered, separate things to pay.

## “Jelenlegi díj” and “Következő számla” — why can they differ?

Two amounts stand side by side on the card, and they **deliberately mean something different**:

- **„Jelenlegi díj”** — what you pay for the **currently running** period. This also includes the module
  that you have already cancelled but still use until the renewal day (that one is paid for).
- **„Következő számla”** — what you will pay on the **next** renewal day. The cancelled
  module is already missing from this.

As long as you have not cancelled anything, the two are the same. If they differ, the difference shows exactly
how much cheaper it will be after the renewal day. In that case the module’s row also shows the exact date
(*“Cancelled — remains active until …”*).

## Items on the next invoice

Under **„A következő számla tételei”** the breakdown is **open by default**: the base fee
and the active modules. (Tapping the label lets you collapse it if you are only interested in the
total.) If you switched on a new module this month, you will see it
with an **„új”** marker — its fee appears for the first time now. The cancelled module does
**not** appear here, since it will no longer be on the next invoice.

## What happens if the fee does not arrive?

We notify you 3 days before renewal by email, and on the renewal day we send a
payment link. If the fee does not arrive, we send a reminder (an email,
then an SMS too), and 10 days after the renewal day we **temporarily
suspend** the website.

In this case a red card stands at the top of the **Modulok** tab: **„A honlapja jelenleg
NEM elérhető”**. On it you see the **exact amount of the outstanding fee to be settled** (this is the
largest figure on the page), with the **„Befizetem”** button and the amount to pay beneath it, and also
the date up to which the fee can be settled. **Nothing is lost:** your modules remain,
they are only paused, and the website reconnects by itself the moment payment is made.

During this time your visitors do not receive an error message, but a polite page with the **name and
contact details of your accommodation** — the guest does not
see the reason for the suspension.

While the suspension lasts you **cannot add a new module**: in place of the
purchase buttons stands the label **„Rendezés után vehető fel”**. However, you can still cancel
your existing modules just as before, and you can also withdraw a cancellation — the
suspension does not restrict these.

When the fee arrives, a **green confirmation** appears in place of the red card
(“Your website is available again”), and we also send an email about it — so you can be sure
that your website has truly returned.

This green card not only says “all is well”, but also tells you **which
period you have paid for**: *“This settles the period 10/09/2031 – 10/09/2032,
HUF 99,900.”* This way you do not have to work out until when your
service is covered. (The amount is only shown there if an invoice also confirms it; if the
document has not yet been created, the sentence omits the amount, or is left out
entirely — we never write a figure there that we cannot confirm.)

Beneath it, a line about the invoice: *“We have sent the invoice by email; automatic
card charging will resume from the next renewal day.”* — and if the invoice has already been
issued, a **link to it opens here**. The link bears your own invoice number
(for example “Open CIT-2031-0042 among the Documents ▸”); tapping it takes you
straight to the **Dokumentumok** tab, filtered to your invoice — you don’t have to search for
the email. If we do not yet know the invoice number, the link stands there
with the label **„Megnyitom a Dokumentumok közt ▸”**; and if there is no document
at all yet, no link appears (we do not promise a page that we cannot open).

## How do I switch to yearly payment?

![Screenshot: the Subscription card with the yearly switch box, on a phone](assets/hu/screen.png)

If you pay monthly, a separate box on the Subscription card shows how much
you would save with yearly payment: **you get 12 months for the price of a few months’ less monthly fee** —
exactly how much and how large the saving is, the box writes out with a figure. Tapping the
**„Váltok éves fizetésre a következő fordulónaptól”** button schedules the switch —
you **do not pay anything now**, and your already-paid period
runs to the end unchanged. On the next renewal day your invoice becomes yearly. (If your
next monthly invoice has already been issued — this can happen in the days before the
renewal day —, it still arrives at the old price, and the switch takes effect from the renewal after it;
the green confirmation always shows the exact date.)

You can change your mind until the renewal day: in the green confirmation you can step back at any time,
without consequence, using the **„Mégsem — maradok a havi fizetésnél”** button. **Once the yearly invoice is paid, the switch is final** — the yearly fee
is for the full year, there is no refund; if you cancel your subscription later, the
paid year runs to its end.

## Automatic card charging — what it means and how to withdraw it

If you paid by bank card, the card is stored by the payment provider (we do not
see it), and we **deduct the fee automatically** on the renewal day — there is nothing for you to do.
3 days before the charge we write by email how much it will be and when. On the
Subscription card you can see whether this is currently **on** or **off**.

If you do not want it, tapping the **„Megbízás visszavonása”** button brings up a
small window that lists what changes as a result; there you apply it with the
**„Igen, visszavonom a megbízást”** button, or everything stays as before with the
**„Mégsem — marad az automatikus fizetés”** button.
We also send an email confirmation of the withdrawal, including what happens on the next
renewal day.

After withdrawal **you have to pay** on every renewal day using the sent
payment link. The obligation to pay the fee remains, and if the fee does not
arrive, the same happens as above: reminders, then a temporary
suspension of the website. Reconnecting is not a single click: because of the
bank card confirmation you can give a new mandate either on the **Pénztárca** tab, using the **„Kártya megadása”** button (this involves a confirmation step, without a purchase), or by
settling the next payment link — that payment also gives the mandate.

Which card is saved (brand, last 4 digits, expiry), and how to
replace it, is shown by the **Pénztárca** tab — the
**„Pénztárca — melyik kártya, csere”** button beneath the card takes you there. A separate guide covers this.

## Automatic card charging has stalled — what should I do?

If the fee could not be deducted from the saved card (the most common reason being that
there were not enough funds on it at the time), the charge **stops**, and the website is suspended after the grace
period. In this case, on the **Modulok** tab, within the **Előfizetés**
card — in its lower half, where the status of automatic charging otherwise stands
— instead of the usual green “ON” label a red
**„NEM SIKERÜLT”** marker stands, with the title **beneath it**:
**„Az automatikus kártyaterhelés elakadt”**.

⚠️ **Important:** the automatic system **does not try again on its own**. If you have topped up
the card in the meantime, the charge will still not run by itself — you have to
start it. That is why there are two buttons here.

### Which button should I choose?

**„Újrapróbálom ezzel a kártyával”** — this is the blue, prominent button. Choose it
if **the same card has become usable in the meantime**: you topped it up,
the bank unblocked it, or whatever caused the first charge to stall has been resolved. One
tap, and we attempt the deduction again — you don’t have to enter the
card number again.

**„Másik kártyával fizetek”** — this is the faint, secondary button. Choose it if
**you want to use a different card**, or if retrying did not lead to a
result. This takes you to the payment page, where you enter the new card. Next to the card
stands the explanation as well: *“The card entered via »Másik kártyával fizetek« becomes the new mandate
— because of bank card confirmation it can only be given this way.”* In other words, you can
re-establish automatic charging **only this way**: under the bank card rules, the saved card can only be brought back by a payment you yourself
initiate and confirm.

> The third, quiet line — **„Megbízás visszavonása”** — is not a payment, but its
> opposite: with this you cancel automatic charging. The outstanding fee
> does **not disappear** as a result, which the screen also states.

### What will I see after retrying?

After pressing the button you return to this page, and **a bar at the top describes what
happened**. You may receive seven different responses, and each means something different:

- **It succeeded.** *“Succeeded — we deducted the fee from the card, and your website is available
  again.”* This is the good news: the money has arrived, the website is visible to
  visitors again. There is nothing further to do.
- **The bank has not yet responded.** *“The charge has started, the bank has not yet responded.”*
  In this case you have to wait. **You don’t have to keep the page open** — if it succeeds, the
  website reconnects by itself, and we send an email about it.
- **The bank declined again.** *“The bank declined the card this time too, so we did
  NOT deduct anything.”* This is important: **no money moved**, we did not charge you
  twice. Try again later, or pay with a different card — there is also a
  button for that in the bar.
- **The grace period still applies.** *“We recently tried with this card.
  You can try again in 15 minutes.”* Between two manual attempts we wait **15 minutes**.
  There is a reason for this: if the bank has just declined, a repeat a few seconds later
  would run into a decline all the same. During the wait you can still pay with a different
  card — there is a button for that in the bar too.
- **Attempts have run out.** *“We have already tried several times with this card, and the
  bank declined each time — we will not attempt it again, so as not to charge you
  unnecessarily.”* There are **four in total** automatic deduction attempts
  per renewal (one for the automatic system, three for you). This is not our strictness: the
  card companies limit the repetition of a declined charge. If the bank
  declined several times, what is missing is not the repetition, but **a different card**.
- **No saved card.** *“There is no saved card with which we could try
  again.”* In this case there is nothing to retry — you settle the fee with the payment button on the red
  card, by bank card.
- **Nothing to settle.** *“There is no outstanding balance to settle — nothing to
  retry.”* This comes when the fee has already arrived in the meantime (for example your
  earlier payment went through). There is nothing to do.

If you see a message different from these (“We could not start the charge right now”),
**write to us** — we reply fastest from the email address given on the Account tab.

## How can I cancel the subscription?

By tapping the **„Előfizetés lemondása…”** line at the bottom of the Modulok tab. The cancellation
takes effect on the renewal day: until then the website runs unchanged — since that
period is already paid for. If you change your mind, you can step back until the renewal day with the **„Meggondoltam magam —
folytatom”** button.

After cancellation the interface everywhere states the closing: the **„Következő számla”** and the Pénztárca’s
**„Következő terhelés”** line show “none”, with this next to it: *“You have cancelled your subscription: it
closes on … . We will not charge you, and will not send a payment link either.”* — and in the sidebar “closes …, we do not
charge”, while the card pill reads **„LEMONDVA — NEM TERHELÜNK”**. You will not receive the “renewing soon” email before the renewal day either.
We send an email confirmation of the cancellation (and, if you step back, of the continuation too).

**The commitment period is an exception.** If you ordered your own web address from us, a commitment period
is attached to it, and while it runs, cancellation involves a settlement: in this case the **„Előfizetés
lemondása…”** button takes you to a separate settlement page, where you see
item by item what is to be paid before you decide. You will find the details in the help topic “Cancellation during the commitment period —
settlement and the fate of the web address”. After a settlement has been paid,
the step-back button is no longer available — in that case, write to us.
